analysis.one_liner: Wipro is an Indian IT services and consulting company that builds, runs and modernises technology systems for large global corporations across banking, healthcare, manufacturing and other sectors.
analysis.whats_happening: Wipro reported Q2 FY27 results on 15 Oct 2026: consolidated revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹24,753 crore, but net profit fell 1.4% YoY to ₹3,201 crore (down ~4.5% sequentially). The headline revenue growth was driven mainly by rupee depreciation - core IT services revenue was flat sequentially and up just 0.6% YoY in constant currency. Operating margin improved to 16.5% from 16%, and the stock rose over 6% on relief at the margin print. A day later, Wipro announced a small $2,000 purchase of a 20% stake in US AI firm FLARRE.AI to build insurance-sector AI capability - a capability tuck-in, not a financially material deal.
analysis.plain_terms: Revenue 'growing 9%' sounds good, but almost all of that is the rupee weakening against the dollar, not Wipro winning more business - the underlying business grew a bare 0.6% over the year. Profit actually fell slightly. The one genuine positive is that margins (how much the company keeps from each rupee of revenue) improved, which is why the stock rallied. The tension is simple: is this a business getting more efficient while waiting for growth to return, or a business papering over weak demand with cost cuts?
analysis.quarters: Reported revenue growth (9.1% YoY) and constant-currency IT services growth (0.6% YoY, flat sequentially) diverge sharply this quarter - the gap is almost entirely currency, not volume; treat the 9.1% figure as non-comparable to prior quarters on a like-for-like basis. Net profit fell 1.4% YoY to ₹3,201 crore even as margin rose to 16.5% (from 16% last quarter), implying cost control is doing the heavy lifting. Large deal bookings ($2.6 billion TCV, 9 deals) hit a 19-quarter low; management said two large deals were awarded but not formally signed in the quarter and should close in Q3. Headcount fell by ~6,716 to about 236,328, with attrition easing slightly to 13.8%. Management guided Q3 FY27 sequential IT services revenue of -1.5% to +0.5%, citing seasonal furloughs and continued softness in the Americas and US healthcare (policy-driven), while still targeting a 17-17.5% margin band with no firm timeline.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 44% from its all-time high of ₹329.53 (4 Jan 2022) and has lagged badly across every horizon: -24.6% over 1 year versus Nifty -9.5% and peer Infosys -18.2%; -3.1% over 3 years versus Nifty +16.8%; -43.1% over 5 years versus Nifty +25.3%. This is a sustained, multi-year underperformance, not a single bad year. Two corporate actions sit inside this period - a 2:1 stock split (Dec 2024) and a ₹15,000 crore buyback at ₹250/share (completed June 2026, above today's price) - but the price series and drawdown figures supplied are already split-adjusted, so no further correction is needed; these were capital-return events, not business distress, though they don't change the underlying fact that long-term holders have lost money in real terms.
analysis.valuation_read: At ₹184.4, Wipro trades around 12.7x trailing earnings and roughly 2.2x book value, well below large IT peers that trade in the high-teens to twenties on P/E. It is cheap relative to the sector because the market is pricing in structurally slower growth (constant-currency IT revenue growth near 0.6% this quarter) than faster-growing peers, not because of any balance-sheet distress. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether that growth rate is a cyclical trough or the new normal - a low multiple on a shrinking growth rate is not automatically a bargain.
analysis.growth_read: This quarter's growth is margin-led, not volume-led: constant-currency IT services revenue was essentially flat (up 0.6% YoY), while operating margin expanded to 16.5% from 16%. Per the company's own commentary, clients are prioritising cost optimisation and AI-led efficiency over fresh discretionary spending, which is consistent with weak volume growth propped up by internal cost control rather than genuine demand expansion - the less durable combination.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk looks low: available data points to a net cash position with debt/equity near 0.23x and debt/EBITDA around 1.1x, and zero promoter pledging. The real question for Wipro is business risk - whether demand recovers - not financial risk. Whether reported profit is converting cleanly into free cash flow this quarter was not independently verifiable from the sources checked - not verified, check the cash flow statement on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Premji family and affiliated trusts/entities) held about 72.6% as of the September 2026 quarter, with 0% pledged - a high and unencumbered insider stake that signals no leverage-driven selling risk at the promoter level. FII/FPI holding rose modestly to 9.46% from 8.85%, while mutual fund holding dipped to 1.66% from 1.83%. No specific marquee non-promoter investor stood out in the data checked.
strengths: Promoter holding of ~72.6% with 0% pledging as of Sept 2026 - high insider alignment, no forced-selling risk
Net cash balance sheet with debt/equity near 0.23x, giving the company room to keep returning capital
Operating margin improved to 16.5% from 16% sequentially in Q2 FY27 despite flat constant-currency revenue
Completed a ₹15,000 crore buyback (60 crore shares at ₹250) in June 2026, directly returning capital to shareholders
watchpoints: Core IT services revenue grew just 0.6% YoY in constant currency this quarter - the reported 9.1% growth is mostly rupee depreciation, not real demand
Large deal bookings of $2.6 billion were a 19-quarter low; management says two deals slipped into Q3 but this needs to be confirmed in bookings, not just rhetoric
Q3 FY27 guidance of -1.5% to +0.5% sequential revenue signals continued near-term softness, particularly in Americas and US healthcare
Stock has underperformed the Nifty and peer Infosys over 1, 3 and 5 years, with no sign yet of a valuation re-rating despite the margin improvement
analysis.one_thing: Whether the $2.6 billion of large deals management says slipped into Q3 actually convert into signed bookings and lift constant-currency IT services revenue meaningfully above the current ~0.6% YoY pace - that would tell us if this is a margin story turning into a growth story, or a margin story masking a growth problem.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue/profit/margin figures cross-checked across Business Today, HDFC Sky, Equentis and an earnings-call transcript (Benzinga/BigGo) - consistent. Valuation ratios (P/E ~12.7x, P/B ~2.2x, ROE ~15.7%, ROCE ~18.5%, debt/equity ~0.23x) came from a stock-screener aggregator; one source's dividend yield figure (6.71%) contradicted the verified 4.34% supplied and was set aside as a stale outlier. The ₹15,000 crore buyback figure was corrected against an apparent 10x typo in one source (which read ₹1,50,000 crore) using the share-count math (60 crore shares x ₹250 = ₹15,000 crore) and a separate source stating the figure explicitly. Operating cash flow conversion from PAT was not independently verified - check on Screener.
